variants.title: Liveness equals readiness
variants.context: A pod is killed because /health fails while the process is only warming a cache.
variants.constraint: The process is alive but not ready for traffic.
variants.question: How should probes be split?
variants.expectedPattern: Liveness means the process should be restarted; readiness means it can receive traffic.
wrongChoices: One probe that kills the pod during warmup
Liveness that hits a slow dependency

variants.title: Health hits the primary database
variants.context: Every 2s probe runs SELECT 1 on the only primary from 300 pods.
variants.question: What should a cheap check do?
variants.expectedPattern: Check local process health (and maybe a pool ping) without amplifying load on the primary.
wrongChoices: Full table scan on every probe
Open a new DB connection per probe with no reuse
Probe every dependency on the user path

variants.title: Always-200 health endpoint
variants.context: /health returns 200 even when the app cannot serve requests because a required dependency is down.
variants.constraint: The load balancer keeps sending traffic.
variants.question: What should readiness reflect?
variants.expectedPattern: Fail readiness when the instance cannot do useful work, so traffic shifts away.
wrongChoices: Crash the process on every blip

variants.title: Deep health causes a cascade
variants.context: Readiness checks the payment vendor; the vendor blips and every pod goes unready at once.
variants.constraint: The site could still serve catalog traffic.
variants.question: How deep should default readiness be?
variants.expectedPattern: Check local critical dependencies, not every optional vendor, or isolate optional features.
wrongChoices: Tie readiness to every third-party ping
Mark the whole site unready on an optional widget
No distinction between critical and optional

variants.title: Startup probe missing
variants.context: A JVM app takes 90s to start, and liveness kills it at 30s in a loop.
variants.question: Which probe covers boot?
variants.expectedPattern: A startup probe (or delayed liveness) so slow boot is not treated as a crash loop.
wrongChoices: Kill on first failed TCP connect

variants.title: Health on the public internet
variants.context: /health exposes internal versions, hostnames, and dependency errors to the world.
variants.question: What belongs on a public probe?
variants.expectedPattern: A minimal authenticated or internal-only check; do not leak internals on a public URL.
wrongChoices: Database credentials in the health JSON

variants.title: Stale success from a sidecar
variants.context: The sidecar answers 200 while the app process is dead.
variants.constraint: Traffic still reaches the pod IP.
variants.question: What must the probe actually test?
variants.expectedPattern: The serving process (or a port that fails when the app is down), not only the sidecar.
wrongChoices: TCP to the sidecar admin port only
Always-ready as long as the pod exists
Kubelet ping of pause container only

variants.title: Flapping readiness
variants.context: A dependency times out every other probe, so the instance flaps in and out of rotation.
variants.question: How do you stabilize probes?
variants.expectedPattern: Thresholds (failure/success counts) and timeouts that ignore brief blips.

variants.title: Exec probe saturates CPU
variants.context: An exec health script forks a shell and a Python interpreter every second on each pod.
variants.constraint: The check is heavier than the app.
variants.question: What probe type is appropriate?
variants.expectedPattern: A cheap HTTP or TCP check in-process, not a heavy exec on every interval.
wrongChoices: shell out to a large script every second

variants.title: Drain ignored
variants.context: A deploy SIGKILLs pods while they are still in the load balancer pool.
variants.question: What sequence should health enable?
variants.expectedPattern: Fail readiness, wait for drain, then stop the process.

variants.title: Synthetic check vs real path
variants.context: Health returns 200, but the only real endpoint needs a missing config file and 500s.
variants.constraint: The probe does not exercise the serving path.
variants.question: What is the gap?
variants.expectedPattern: Readiness should verify the process can serve its critical path, not a dummy string.

variants.title: Multi-port service
variants.context: Metrics port is up, HTTP API port is down, and the balancer uses the metrics port as health.
variants.question: Which port should readiness use?
variants.expectedPattern: Probe the user-facing port and protocol, not a side port that can be healthy independently.

variants.title: Health check storm after deploy
variants.context: A mesh retries probes from every sidecar at once and the new pods never become ready.
variants.question: How do you keep probes from becoming load?
variants.expectedPattern: Bound probe rate and cost so health traffic cannot prevent readiness.
wrongChoices: Probe the production database with heavy queries at deploy

variants.title: Dependency timeout longer than probe timeout
variants.context: Readiness waits 10s on a 30s downstream timeout and probes overlap until threads exhaust.
variants.question: What timeout rule applies?
variants.expectedPattern: Health checks must use short timeouts and bounded concurrency, shorter than the probe period.

variants.title: False healthy during deadlock
variants.context: The health thread is separate and still answers 200 while request threads are deadlocked.
variants.constraint: Users are stuck; probes are green.
variants.question: What should liveness detect?
variants.expectedPattern: A check that fails if the request path cannot make progress (watchdog), not only a side thread.
wrongChoices: A dedicated thread that always returns 200
Health in a process that never serves traffic
